name: Foggia (Main)
note: I./KG 76 "withdrew to Foggia in Italy" on 16/17 May 1943 and abandoned the base in September (Wikipedia, Kampfgeschwader 76, citing de Zeng, Stankey and Creek 2008, pp. 234-235). Which of the Foggia fields it used is not given there: the mark is the main airfield, the complex's centre (assumed). Position: Wikipedia, Foggia Airfield Complex.

name: Foggia (Main)
note: II./KG 76 "deployed south to Foggia on the 18 July" (same source). Field within the complex assumed, as above.

name: La Sebala II
note: Consolidated at La Sebala II after 13 May 1943, "mounting only defensive patrols against Axis bombers"; patrols from La Sebala and, from 28 May, Monastir (Wikipedia, No. 255 Squadron RAF, citing the squadron's record book, TNA AIR 27/1518, folios 186-192); Beaufighters with Mk VIII AI from 3 July; to Sicily by 17 July. The position is La Sebala airfield's (Wikipedia); La Sebala I and II were neighbouring strips (assumed).

name: La Sebala
note: Station list: La Sebala Airfield, Tunisia, 20 May 1943; Bocca di Falco, Sicily, 1 August 1943 (Wikipedia, 4th Fighter Squadron, from Maurer's Combat Squadrons of the Air Force). Day fighters: whether they met the night raids is not recorded here. The group's 2d and 5th Squadrons, also Spitfires under No. 242 Group (NACAF order of battle, 10 July 1943), are not yet placed.

name: Monastir
note: Patrols "from both La Sebala and Monastir from 28 May 1943" (as above).
